title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: A dysprosocenium cation [(Cp^iPr5)Dy(Cp*)]+ raised the hysteresis temperature to 80 K, above the 77 K boiling point of liquid nitrogen, with Ueff of 1541 cm^-1, the highest-performing SMM highlighted in this review.
explanation: The abstract and Section 5.2 identify terbium- and dysprosium-based progress culminating in Guo's mixed cyclopentadienyl Dy complex: TB increased from a previous 60 K benchmark to 80 K, with Ueff 1541 cm^-1, and hysteresis loops expanded at 77 K. The authors attribute such high Ueff and TB to strong single-ion anisotropy from lanthanide spin-orbit coupling and to ligand-field modulation.
scope: The organometallic Dy single-ion magnet [(Cp^iPr5)Dy(Cp*)][B(C6F5)4] as the record case in this review.
conditions: Hysteresis comparison is at 77 K as shown for this salt; Cp^iPr5 is penta-isopropylcyclopentadienyl and Cp* is pentamethylcyclopentadienyl.
caveats: The abstract pairs 'terbium- and dysprosium-based SMMs' with 1541 cm^-1 and 80 K; the detailed attribution in Section 5.2 is to this Dy complex. The result is molecule-specific.
